records.title: Advanced Resistive Exercise Device (ARED)
records.summary: Uses vacuum cylinders to create loads up to about 270 kg for squats and deadlifts on the ISS.

records.title: T2 treadmill
records.summary: Crew run with a harness and bungees pulling them onto the belt.

records.title: Cycle ergometer (CEVIS)
records.summary: Pedalling without a seat; used for aerobic training and fitness tests.

records.title: Lower body negative pressure
records.summary: Pulls fluid back toward the legs; studied for SANS.

records.title: Thigh cuffs (Braslet)
records.summary: Tight cuffs around the thighs that reduce headward fluid shift; used by Russian crews.

records.title: Fluid and salt loading
records.summary: Salt tablets with water before re-entry to restore blood volume.

records.title: Compression garments
records.summary: Worn during landing and recovery to stop blood pooling in the legs.

records.title: Circadian lighting
records.summary: ISS LED lighting shifts colour and intensity to help keep the body clock in sync.

records.title: Private family conferences
records.summary: Regular private calls and video with family.

records.title: Ground psychological support
records.summary: Regular private conferences with behavioural health specialists.

records.title: Onboard ultrasound
records.summary: Crew trained to scan with remote guidance from Earth; used for eyes, kidneys, heart and more.

records.title: Personal and area dosimetry
records.summary: Passive dosimeters worn by each crew member plus active instruments that warn of solar events.

records.title: Storm shelter
records.summary: The most shielded part of the vehicle, made more so by surrounding the crew with water and supplies.
